finding: Model 1's Earth check depends on a modelling choice. With a different starting assumption about the blow-off slope it predicts 14.3% (13.9–16.1%) and fails.
action: Confirmed with our own rerun. Model 1's pass is labelled weak and the forecast leans on Model 2.

finding: The lunar limit at 14.7 psia and the gravity penalty mostly restate NASA's 1/6-g aircraft tests, which are in the training data. The stated probability of 1.00 was built into the constraints.
action: Reworded: these are NASA measurements that the models reproduce, not predictions. The probability claim is removed.

finding: “No fire experiment in lunar gravity” is wrong. Aircraft and drop-tower tests have reached lunar gravity for seconds at a time.
action: Changed everywhere to “no fire experiment has run on the Moon”.

finding: Short aircraft tests can bias low-gravity limits low: a flame that has not yet died when the 20 seconds end counts as burning. That would overstate the penalty.
action: Added as a stated risk and made into Forecast 2, which a long lunar test will settle.

finding: Model 2 had no floor on the starved side. It allowed cellulose to burn below 10% oxygen in weak drafts, which contradicts the evidence.
action: Model 2 is no longer shown below its data. With a floor added the results barely move: Earth check 15.8%, habitat limit 15.7%.

finding: The pressure step depends on an assumed reaction order, which was mislabelled in the code.
action: Label fixed. Under the alternative assumption the habitat limit is 14.5% instead of 15.4%, so the forecast range was widened to cover both.

finding: The two models share the same evidence, so their agreement is not independent confirmation. The Earth check mainly rules out “gravity has no effect”.
action: Now stated next to the checks and the forecast table.

finding: Paper with an Earth limit near 16% will obviously burn in 34% oxygen. No model is needed for that.
action: Agreed. The habitat result is framed as a sanity check, and the scorable part is the number.
